statusText: Mapped policy state: EA_ON. All 24 published hours fall inside the scheduled weekend halt of CME equity-index futures and the NAS100 CFD, so no pathological Nasdaq-100 price path can form inside the window. Stress remains in the elevated band because the rate, energy and diplomatic questions behind it are unresolved, not because any drawdown was observed.

headline: Nasdaq-100 sits inside the scheduled CME weekend closure after an orderly Friday advance; Tail holds near its floor while post-crisis long-end yields, $92 crude and an unconfirmed Hormuz rejection keep Stress in the elevated band
body:
Every Nasdaq-100 venue has been shut since the Friday 21:00Z settle, and the whole 24-hour published window closes sixteen hours before CME equity-index futures and the NAS100 CFD reopen at 22:00Z on Sunday. Friday's session was orderly and two-sided: cash NDX closed 30,608.14, up 129.28 points or 0.42%, inside a 30,413.59-30,667.56 range and about 0.19% below the session high, against a 30,478.86 previous close. NQ December 2026 futures settled 30,889.25, up 122.50 or 0.40%, within a 30,679.00-30,997.25 range. VIX fell 5.11% to 14.87 in a 14.68-15.94 range. All three major US averages posted weekly gains: the Dow rose 478.64 points or 0.93% to 51,828.62 and snapped a three-week losing streak, the S&P 500 rose 0.51% to 7,743.41 and the Nasdaq Composite rose 0.48% to 27,068.72. Retracements occurred repeatedly through the session and the index did not hold an extreme into the close, so none of the mean-reversion-failure amplifiers this contract requires were present when the tape stopped.

The cross-asset backdrop is the reason Stress sits well above Tail. The Federal Reserve H.15 release shows the 2-year at 4.87%, the 10-year at 5.18% and the 30-year at 5.47% for its latest September 24 column; the 10-year printed 5.225% intraday during the week, its highest since 2007, and the 30-year reached its highest since 2004. WTI November futures settled $92.41, down 2.33%, on optimism around a possible Hormuz reopening. Index internals were dispersed rather than one-way, with MSFT up 3.66% while META fell 3.33%, which is evidence against a single-direction basket rather than for one.

The diplomatic picture is the one item that has shifted since the previous assessment, and it has shifted toward less certainty rather than more. Iran's offer to reopen the Strait of Hormuz within seven days, conveyed via Qatari mediators, was reported by the Wall Street Journal to have been rejected by President Trump, who is described as expecting a renewed bombing campaign after the November midterm elections. Tehran states it is still awaiting an official US response and Reuters has not independently confirmed the rejection, so the near-term de-escalation path is impaired rather than closed. Under this contract a development of that kind raises Stress and informs Confidence; it does not mechanically raise Tail, because Tail requires an observed pathological price path and no venue is open to produce one.

The shared Finviz context file was read at the start of this run and was not used as evidence. Its generatedAt of 2026-09-26T02:04:02Z is more than four hours old, past the 90-minute freshness limit, its collectionStatus is partial, and its futures and calendar sections are both unavailable, so the assessment rests entirely on independent verified research. The forward calendar is heavy but entirely outside this window: August PCE and final Q2 GDP on Wednesday, ISM manufacturing and jobless claims on Thursday, and September nonfarm payrolls on Friday, all carried in the event array as checkpoints rather than as scored risk.

lookbackSummary: Across the trailing 24 published hours the Claude state ranged between Tail 8 and 22 and never reached the block threshold. The September 25 European and US cash stretch from 06:00Z to 14:00Z produced four trend-up prints and a run of WATCH states at Tail 20-22 as the index worked higher; the 13:00Z slot has no published assessment and is marked unavailable rather than reconstructed. From 15:00Z conditions settled back to mixed at Tail 18-19, and the final eight hours fell to Tail 12, 10, 10, 9, 9, 8, 8 and 8 as the Friday settle passed and the weekend closure began. Stress ran between 44 and 57 throughout, consistently above Tail, which is the intended separation: the trailing window contained a difficult high-yield environment, not a pathological price path.
outlookSummary: The entire published window falls inside the scheduled weekend closure: futures settled at 21:00Z on Friday and do not reopen until 22:00Z on Sunday, sixteen hours past the final slot. Tail is held between 7 and 10 for all 24 hours because sustained mean-reversion failure requires a tradable price path, and none of the inherited amplifiers, shallow or failed retracements, repeated extension, or an index pinned near an extreme, can be observed while every Nasdaq-100 venue is shut. Tail eases to 7 through the middle of Saturday, when the reopen is furthest away, then firms to 9 and 10 across the early Sunday hours on reopen proximity alone rather than on any observation. Stress traces a mirror path, easing from 46 to 43 through the quietest weekend hours and firming to 50 by the final slot as the reopen and Wednesday's August PCE draw nearer. Confidence decays from 84 to 78 because the newest verified Nasdaq-100 observation keeps ageing with nothing able to replace it. Every hour maps to EA_ON and green, and the reopen gap itself lies outside this forecast.
